issues.description: The DD.weight attribute is annotated as a float in the template dd.py, but the decision-diagram design, problem statement, and the solution use complex weights (np.complex128) throughout (terminals and operations). This type-annotation mismatch can confuse students (and static type checkers) about the intended weight type and may lead to incorrect assumptions when implementing functions that rely on complex amplitudes.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the DD.weight annotation in the template consistent with the intended design by using a complex type (e.g., np.complex128 or complex) instead of float. Update the annotation in template dd.py to `weight: np.complex128` (or `complex`) and ensure any related type hints/comments mention complex amplitudes so students and type-checkers see the intended usage.
